about: Hand-labeled ground truth for measuring retrieval accuracy. Run it with: python -m bench.run
Every row names a video in the library, a query, and what a correct answer looks like:
expect.start / expect.end  a true interval in seconds, scored by temporal IoU
expect.text                the exact characters a text-reading query should return
To add a row: play the video in the app, note when the event really starts and ends,
and append an entry with a unique id. Ten careful rows beat fifty careless ones - the
metrics are only ever as trustworthy as these labels.
label_confidence is a note to yourself. 'high' means the boundaries were checked by eye;
'approximate' means the row is a placeholder worth tightening before you trust a delta.

rows.query: what file name is shown in the editor tab?
rows.note: Read off the frames at 2s and 18s: the active editor tab is ModifiedDFC_2_T4.ipynb. Both the pre-SigLIP and post-SigLIP runs hallucinated different names here, which is the point of the row. The earlier label was itself taken from a model answer - never do that.

rows.query: scrolling through code in an editor
rows.note: The clip is one continuous scroll, so almost any overlapping answer is defensible. Tighten this if you want the row to discriminate.

rows.query: a robot climbing a vertical pole
rows.note: Taken from the indexed scene description rather than checked by eye. Verify and tighten before trusting it.
